# Introduction {#sec-intro}

The Sleeping Beauty problem has been with us for a while [@haugerud2001, 34].
@renner-alvi2023 [119] thinks it is still open, and so do others
[see @batzorig2019, ch. 2; @tanaka2025]. @Sec-model sets out a model, and
@sec-results states the main results. The longer proofs are in
@sec-proofs.^[A footnote, placed after the punctuation, as the guide asks.]

Here is a quotation long enough to be set as a block:

> [The thirder] is committed to the claim that an agent can lower her
> credence in a proposition without acquiring any evidence against it,
> merely by coming to occupy one of several centered worlds compatible with
> what she already believed. ... Whether that is a reductio or a discovery is
> precisely what is at issue. [@renner-alvi2023, 119]

And an inline one: "a case in which learning nothing is not the same as
learning that nothing has happened" [@haugerud2001, 34].

# The model {#sec-model}

::: {#def-vigil}
## Vigil
A *Vigil* is a triple $\langle W, \mathrm{Cr}, \tau \rangle$ in which $W$ is
a finite set of centered worlds, $\mathrm{Cr}$ a probability measure on
$\mathcal{P}(W)$, and $\tau \colon W \to \mathbb{N}$ assigns to each world
the number of times the agent is woken in it.
:::

The update rule we care about is
$$
\mathrm{Cr}^{+}(A) = \frac{\sum_{w \in A} \tau(w)\,\mathrm{Cr}(\{w\})}
                          {\sum_{w \in W} \tau(w)\,\mathrm{Cr}(\{w\})},
$$ {#eq-proportional}
where $\mathrm{Cr}^{+}$ is the credence on waking. @Fig-credence plots what
@eq-proportional says about heads as the number of tails wakings grows.

![Credence in heads under @eq-proportional, by the number of wakings if the coin lands tails.](credence.pdf){#fig-credence width=70%}

# Results {#sec-results}

::: {#lem-weights}
Each waking in a Vigil in which $\tau$ is constant on $T$ has the same weight.
:::

::: {#prp-thirder}
## Thirder
Let $\langle W, \mathrm{Cr}, \tau\rangle$ be a Vigil in which $\tau$ takes
exactly the values $1$ and $2$. If credence on waking is proportional to
$\tau$, credence in heads is $1/3$.
:::

::: {.proof}
By @lem-weights the three wakings are equiprobable, and exactly one of them
is in $H$.
:::

::: {#thm-convergence}
Let $\langle W, \mathrm{Cr}, \tau \rangle$ be a Vigil with $\tau(w) \leq k$
for every $w \in W$. Then iterated proportional updating converges, and its
limit is independent of $\mathrm{Cr}$.
:::

@thm-convergence is proved in @sec-proofs. @Tbl-credences compares the rules,
and @Prp-thirder is the familiar thirder verdict.

::: {#tbl-credences}

| Rule          | Prior | On waking | After learning it is Monday |
|:--------------|:-----:|:---------:|:---------------------------:|
| Halfer        | $1/2$ | $1/2$     | $2/3$                       |
| Thirder       | $1/2$ | $1/3$     | $1/2$                       |
| Double halfer | $1/2$ | $1/2$     | $1/2$                       |

Credence in heads under three rules.

:::

# Proofs {#sec-proofs .appendix}

::: {.restate ref="thm-convergence"}
:::

::: {.proof}
Since $\tau$ is bounded by $k$ and $W$ is finite, the map
$\mathrm{Cr} \mapsto \mathrm{Cr}^{+}$ defined by @eq-proportional is a
continuous self-map of the simplex, and the rest is Banach.
:::
